body: Doire mhòr, which had refused the first contract and then lost its water, has by now only a few households. The beacon of the stoppage was lit on its hill by the descendants of Beathag Dhubh's people, and the constables burn the hill's heather to deny it to them.

title: Fewer ships from the west
body: The keepers' daybooks at the five beacons record fewer ships arriving from an Tìr Thall each year, and the ships that come are older. The Company's letters speak of troubles at home that they do not describe.

title: Caol leathan's idle harbour
body: At Caol leathan the wool-ships for the humans' market wait for cargo space that does not come. The merchants of the town begin selling their wool inland again, by barter, which is illegal.

title: Caol bheag's empty quay
body: The Company's quay at Caol bheag on the northern coast, built for the eastern trade, handles one ship in a season. The Company's agent there writes that he has been forgotten.

title: Imperial overreach begins openly
body: Human administrators begin issuing directives with no Rodian counsel sought at all — the polite fiction of permission finally dropped.

title: Lionel Strake Commissioner
body: Charles Merriman leaves Rodos in ill health. Lionel Strake, a soldier, replaces him. His commission, read aloud at the Residency, makes no mention of the Council of Custodians, and he does not call on it.

title: The council locked out
body: Strake has the council hall at Cathair dhearg locked and its keys lodged at the Residency. The custodians meet instead in the Dark Unicorn's temple, whose priests, who had blessed the humans' coin, now shelter those who had petitioned against it.

title: The confiscation edict
body: Human authorities formally claim the right to seize any Rodian dwelling deemed necessary for extraction expansion. It is the single most-cited grievance in every surviving account of what came next.

title: The seizure of Doire mhòr
body: The first dwellings taken under the edict are those of Doire mhòr, for a new shaft beneath the hill. The last households are carried out by constables. The village that refused the first contract is the first to be emptied by the last.

title: Evictions at Baile dhomhain
body: At Baile dhomhain, the first camp laid out on paper, two streets are pulled down for a spoil-tip. The families are offered huts at Àth ìseal and marks for their timber; most go to kin in the hill villages instead.

title: Mòrag Maor lays down the staff
body: Mòrag nic Iain Maor, fourth of her line to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, refuses to carry out evictions in her district and breaks the staff at the Company's door. Three other overseers resign in the same month. The Company appoints humans to their places.

title: The silver guild arms
body: The silver guild of Muileann chiar, still holding its seam under the compact made a century before, begins buying rifles through the eastern pirates. Its ledger enters them as refining tools.

title: Rifles by way of the pirates
body: The rifles for the silver guild come ashore from the raiders' boats in the eastern waters, where no Company gunboat has patrolled for years. The raiders take payment in silver bar, by weight.

title: The council at Cnoc bheag forest
body: Custodians, crew-leaders of the Lamp-Watch and the dissenting priests of the Dark Unicorn meet in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag and form a single council for the mining regions. Eilidh nic Raghnaill is chosen to speak for it. The meeting is not recorded by any human source.

title: The arrest order
body: Strake orders the arrest of Eilidh nic Raghnaill and the members of the forest council. The constables go to Baile thais and find the house empty and the town silent.

title: War declared
body: Rodian resistance, coordinated for the first time across multiple mining regions, moves from grievance to open conflict.

title: The stores taken at Muileann chrom
body: The war opens in the hills. At Muileann chrom the fortified store is rushed at first light by crews under Mòrag nic Iain, and its eleven constables surrender without a shot fired. The store's rifles and its grain are carried off before noon.

title: The quay at Ceann fhada seized
body: Crews from the camps take the Company's ore quay at Ceann fhada and sink two barges across its mouth. No ore leaves the hills by water again in the age.

title: The siege of the store at Baile thais
body: At Baile thais the constables hold their walled pithead against the town for eleven days, the same span as the first strike a lifetime before. They surrender on the twelfth, when their water runs out. Eilidh nic Raghnaill sends them under guard to the coast unharmed, an order the Residency did not expect and did not reciprocate.

title: The northern pits rise
body: The crews at Baile gharbh and the northern pits rise in the same week, take the constable posts at Muileann shean and Tobar ghorm, and send the constables south on foot.

title: The ore road cut
body: Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, closes the gates of the house across the ore road, and the men in its loft come down armed. The road between the capital and the hills is cut at its halfway stage and stays cut.

title: Uilleam Gobha's forge
body: At Muileann dhearg the smith Uilleam Gobha turns the Company's own blasting-powder into grenades cased in ore-tin, and forges pike-heads from rails torn up in the galleries. The rebels' council records that it could not have fought its first season without him.

title: The capital rises
body: At Cathair dhearg the custodians break the Residency's locks on their council hall and sit in it again. The townsfolk hold Drochaid Cathair dhearg against the constables sent up from the harbour, and the bridge built for ore-carts is barricaded with them.

title: Cathair dhomhain joins
body: At Cathair dhomhain the townsfolk break open the Company's warehouse, the first building on Rodos the Company ever owned, and carry off its tools for the council's companies.

title: Muileann mhin takes sides
body: At Muileann mhin, a river port just east of the capital, the townsfolk argue for three days and then send boats to the council. The boats carry food down the Abhainn fhionn to the capital through the winter.

title: The Residency fortified
body: Lionel Strake withdraws the Administration into the Residency above Ros dhomhain and fortifies the Company's quarter of the harbour. The city below it, overwhelmingly Ròdaich, neither joins the rising nor opposes it, and the constables do not trust it enough to leave the walls.

title: The fight at the ford of Àth chiar
body: A column of constables and Company guards under Major Peter Ashdown marches up the ore road to relieve the hills and is met at the ford of Àth chiar. The rebels hold the far bank. Ashdown loses forty men and his baggage and turns back; the rebels lose nineteen, whose names the council's roll gives in full.

title: Ashdown's retreat through Dùn chrom
body: Ashdown's column falls back through Dùn chrom and stops at the barracks there for a night. In the morning the town has closed its gates behind them, and the column continues to the coast without its wounded, whom the townsfolk keep and nurse.

title: The silver town rises
body: The silver guild of Muileann chiar declares for the council and opens its armoury. The Company agents in the town are escorted to the coast with their papers. It is the only place on the island where the rising took nothing, the guild's ledger notes, because the humans had never held anything there to take.

title: The surrender at Dùn ìseal
body: The small constabulary post at Dùn ìseal, cut off by the rising at the silver town, surrenders to the silver guild's riflemen after a single exchange of fire. The east of the island is clear of human arms.

title: Dùn dhearg declares
body: The custodians of Dùn dhearg declare for the council and send it grain. It is the town whose custodian had written the only surviving defence of the Small-Burning Law, and the declaration quotes it.

title: Cnoc leathan's riflemen
body: Riflemen raised at Cnoc leathan in the east join the silver guild's companies and garrison the eastern road. The Company's carters on the road are allowed to go home with their carts.

title: The eastern pits at Ros fhionn
body: The crews of the eastern workings around Ros fhionn stop the pumps and walk out, letting the lower galleries flood. The Company's engineers there go down the Abhainn chaol and take ship at Seann Mhorn for Ros dhomhain. The bridge on the eastern ore road falls silent.

title: Seann Toll shelled
body: A Company steamship, come up the Abhainn uaine, shells the ore stage at Seann Toll to deny it to the rebels, and sets the fishing town behind it burning. Twenty-three townsfolk die. It is the first time the humans turn the island's own ore, burning in their boilers, against a Ròdaich town.

title: Coaling from Inis mhòr
body: The Company steamships coal from the ore stacked on the quays of Inis mhòr, the river port just east of the capital, which its barges carry down the Abhainn fhionn to the ships at Cathair dhomhain. Townsfolk set the stacks alight. The ships put in at Ros dhomhain instead, and burn their own stores.

title: The fishermen of Seann Chwen
body: Fishing boats from Seann Chwen and Ros ruadh, sailing by night along the south coast, board a Company coaster at anchor and burn her. The Company withdraws its coastal shipping to the harbours of Ros dhomhain and Ros bheag.

title: The other Seann Chwen
body: The fishermen of the other Seann Chwen, on the south coast further west, join the raids along the shore. The record keeps the two towns apart by naming their boats.

title: Cathair gheal behind its walls
body: The human town of Cathair gheal, on the northern concession, closes its gates and raises a militia, but sends none of it south to the Residency. Its magistrate writes to both sides asking to be left alone. The council grants it; Strake does not reply.

title: Muileann àrsaidh closes its road
body: The concession town of Muileann àrsaidh closes its road with carts and keeps a watch on it, against both sides. No one attacks it. The watch is kept for the rest of the war.

title: The hawk-shrines open
body: Ìomhar Seabhag declares from the shrine at Seann Skell that the war is Mòd's own hunger turned back on those who fed it. Hawk-shrines across the west become recruiting houses, and a company of the hawk-faithful marches south to join the council.

title: The hawk company at Seann Skell
body: The company of the hawk-faithful is mustered at Seann Skell, the western city, from which the human port of Ros bheag lies a short march to the south-west. It holds the road between Ros bheag and the north-west for the rest of the war.

title: The southern beacon dark
body: The keepers at Tobar dhearg put out the beacon, and the keepers at Àth dhearg and Baile ìseal follow. Company ships feeling their way along the coast by night run on the reefs the beacons were built to light, and two are lost.

title: No relief from the west
body: The Administration's letter-books record repeated requests for troops and ships from an Tìr Thall. One ship arrives in the whole first year of the war, carrying dispatches and a few crates of cartridges, and sails again within the week.

title: The winter lines
body: Through the first winter of the war the council holds the hills, the east and the capital; Strake holds the Residency, the quarter of the harbour below it, and the western ports. Neither side has the strength to attack the other.

title: Grain from Seann Warr
body: The farming town of Seann Warr in the south-east, not the salt port of the same name in the west, sends grain to the hills through the winter by the eastern roads. The council's roll lists the carts.

title: Hunger in the capital
body: Cathair dhearg goes short through the winter, its harbour held by the Residency. The custodians share out the grain by household. The roll records that the custodians took the same share as everyone else.

title: The burning of the third currency's records
body: Rebels destroy the human administration's tithe ledgers in three separate raids — an act later chroniclers treat as symbolically decisive even though its practical effect was small.

title: The counting-house at Ros dhomhain
body: The first raid was on the Company's counting-house at the Ros dhomhain quay, inside the lines. Men of the harbour quarter led by Dùghall Dubh came in over the roofs, carried the tithe books into the yard and burned them.

title: The tithe-house at Ceann àrsaidh
body: The second raid burned the Administration's tithe-house at Ceann àrsaidh, where the portion owed by every settlement in the hills had been entered since the first schedule. The clerks were let go. The custodians of Ceann àrsaidh asked that one ledger be spared for the record, and were refused by their own people.

title: The weigh-house at Muileann chrom
body: The third raid burned the Company's weigh-house at Muileann chrom with its steelyard ledgers. The ore of the hills since the first contract had been entered there by the ton. The rebels' own chronicler writes that the fire burned green.

title: The fight at Cnoc ghorm
body: Company guards and constables sallying from the capital's harbour to recover the eastern road are driven back at Cnoc ghorm, in the hills beyond the capital. It is the last attempt of the war by the Administration to reach the mining district.

title: The harbour quarter changes sides
body: The Ròdaich of the Ros dhomhain harbour quarter, after the counting-house raid, open the lower gates to the council's companies. Strake is left holding the Residency and the Company's quays alone.

title: Cuan uaine opens its quays
body: The river quays of Cuan uaine, east of the capital, open to the council's boats. With them and the Ros dhomhain harbour quarter both lost, the Residency can be supplied only by sea.

title: Strake abandons the Residency
body: Lionel Strake evacuates the Residency by sea with his officials, the Mission's clergy and the Company's agents, and removes the Administration to Ros bheag. The council's companies enter the Residency the next morning and find it stripped of everything but its furniture.

title: Ros bheag the last seat
body: At Ros bheag, the western port the humans had used since the early years, Strake sets up what remains of the Administration. The human families of the west and the south, a few thousand in all, gather behind its walls.

title: Outposts at Ros àrsaidh
body: Strake posts constables at Ros àrsaidh, north of Ros bheag, to hold the coast road. The townsfolk bring them food and news, and the news is always a day old.

title: Hunger in Ros bheag
body: With the roads cut and no ships from the west, Ros bheag runs short of food within months. The Company's stores are opened to the human families and to the Ròdaich townsfolk alike, on Strake's order, the one act of his that the Ròdaich record credits.

title: Cuan shean refuses the humans
body: The custodians of Cuan shean, the town where the first humans came ashore, close its harbour to Company ships. The council's roll notes the irony without comment.

title: The families of Baile dhìreach
body: At Baile dhìreach the descendants of the old joint council, many of them of both peoples, are asked by each side which they are. The record says most of them refused to answer, and that neither side forced them.

title: The last ship from the west
body: The last ship recorded arriving from an Tìr Thall anchors at Ros bheag. She brings no troops and no grain, only a sealed letter for the Commissioner, and she sails again on the next tide with as many passengers as she can hold.

title: The truce of Àth àrsaidh
body: Envoys of the council and of the Administration meet at Àth àrsaidh, on the edge of the northern concession. They agree a truce: the humans remaining on Rodos to withdraw into the north-west under the council's safe-conduct, the council to leave the concession towns standing.

title: Baile Mòr ruadh receives the columns
body: Baile Mòr ruadh, the largest town of the north-west, is named in the truce as the place where the columns will be received. Its Ròdaich people are given the choice of staying or going south. The record gives the numbers of each and they are close.

title: The columns go north
body: The human families of Ros bheag, Cuan shean, Baile dhìreach and the south-west march north along the western roads under guard of the council's companies. Few of them had ever lived in the north. The roll records that no column was attacked, and that none was helped.

title: The columns at Àth chrom
body: The columns cross the ford at Àth chrom on the way north. The custodians of the town stand at the ford and count them over, and the count is the last the Ròdaich make of the humans on Rodos in this age.

title: Àth leathan
body: At Àth leathan, on the last stage before the northern territory, the columns camp for a night. The custodians of the town record that the humans asked the name of the place, and that the name was written down by several of them.

title: The ship that sailed west
body: Lionel Strake, the last Commissioner, sails west from Cuan shean with his officials in the last ship on the island that could make the crossing. The keeper at Taigh-solais Baile chrom records her passing in his daybook. Nothing on Rodos records her arriving anywhere.

title: The beacons relit
body: The council orders the five beacons lit again, from Baile chrom round to Tobar dhearg. The keepers' daybooks, which had counted human ships since the ring was finished, continue to be kept, with nothing in them.

title: The rolls sent to Muileann chaol
body: The custodians send what survives of the age's rolls, their copies of the petitions, the book of Baile thais and the letter-books left in the Residency, to the cellars at Muileann chaol. What the Administration's own clerks carried west with Strake is not known.

title: The Severance
body: The war ends with the crossing itself closed. Whatever let humans reach Rodos shuts. The humans still on the island are shepherded to the northern territory their descendants hold today. Cian and Lorccan, not yet twenty, grow up in its immediate wake.
